proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.

proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance and renews millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 18.487 mills ($18.487 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance and renews millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 18.487 mills ($18.487 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Clinton Community Schools, Lenawee and Washtenaw Counties, Michigan, be renewed for a period of 6 years, 2027 to 2032, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 18 mills are levied in 2027 is approximately $1,580,000 (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy)?
proposals.officialTitle: CLINTON COMMUNITY SCHOOLS OPERATING MILLAGE RENEWAL PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 18 mills for 6 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall the previous voted increase in the tax limitations imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution in Village of Cement City, of 4.9665 mills ($4.9665 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to 4.8542 mills ($4.2852 mills per $1,000 of taxable value) by the require millage rollbacks be renewed at and increased up to the original voted 4.9665 mills ($4.9665 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for 2 years, 2027 through 2028 inclusive, for general operating expenses for the Village of Cement City, raising an estimated fifty five thousand four hundred fifty dollars ($55,450) in the first year the millage is levied?
proposals.officialTitle: Village of Cement City Extra Operating Millage Renewal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 4.9665 mills for 2 years — generally no increase over what you pay now, plus the restored or added amount described.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.
